title: Homogeneous Glycoconjugate Produced by Combined Unnatural Amino Acid Incorporation and Click-Chemistry for Vaccine Purposes
protocol: Dissolve 500 mg of Boc-L-Lys-OH in a mixture of aqueous 1 M NaOH and THF.
Cool the flask in an ice bath.
Add propargyl chloroformate dropwise over a 2-3 min period using a microsyringe while stirring.
Warm the reaction mixture to room temperature and continue stirring for 10 h.
Cool solutions of diethyl ether, aqueous 1 M hydrochloric acid, and ethyl acetate in an ice bath.
Pour the crude reaction mixture into a separation funnel after cooling it in an ice bath.
Extract the mixture with 50 mL of diethyl ether.
Discard the organic layer.
Cautiously add aqueous 1 M hydrochloric acid to the aqueous phase in the separation funnel.
Extract the aqueous layer twice using 30 mL of ethyl acetate.
Verify the presence of N-Boc-propargyl-lysine in the organic phase by TLC.
Dry the combined organic layers over MgSO4.
Filter off the solid phase and concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure on a rotary evaporator.
Dissolve a sample of the crude oily Nα-Boc-propargyl-lysine in deuterated chloroform (CDCl3).
Control its identity by 1H NMR.
Introduce Nα-Boc-propargyl-lysine in a round bottom flask equipped with a septum.
Add 4 mL of anhydrous dichloromethane to the flask under argon to dissolve the Nα-Boc-propargyl-lysine.
Add 4 mL of trifluoroacetic acid dropwise using a syringe while stirring.
Stir the reaction mixture for 1 h at room temperature.
Monitor the reaction by TLC using CH2Cl2-methanol (9:1) as eluent.
Concentrate the reaction mixture under reduced pressure.
Add diethyl ether to the crude residue and incubate it at 4 °C for 1 h to precipitate the PrK.
Filter the PrK in the form of a white solid on a fritted-glass.
Dissolve an aliquot of the PrK in D2O.
Carry out NMR analyses to control its identity and purity.
Dissolve the unnatural amino acid PrK in distilled water at a final concentration of 100 mM.
Store the solution as 1 mL aliquots at -20 °C.
Construct an expression plasmid (pET24d-mPsaAK32TAG-ENLYFQ-HHHHHH) by cloning the target mature Pneumococcal surface adhesin A (mPsaA) gene into pET24d between BamHI and XhoI sites.
Introduce a Tobacco Etch Virus (TEV) protease sequence after mPsaA in the plasmid.
Replace lysine-32 codon with amber codon (TAG).
Construct a second expression plasmid (pEVOL-MmPylRS) containing two copies of MmPylRS gene and tRNAPyr gene.
Thaw a 100 µL aliquot of chemically competent Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) on ice for 5 min.
Add 1 µL of each plasmid (50-100 ng of each) into the cells and incubate for 30 min on ice.
Transfer the microtube with the thawed competent cells to an incubator at 42 °C for 45 s.
Move the microtube back to ice for 2 min.
Add 900 µL of LB medium and incubate under shaking for 1 h at 37 °C to allow antibiotic expression.
Plate the bacteria onto LB agar with 25 µg/mL of kanamycin and 30 µg/mL of chloramphenicol.
Allow bacteria growth overnight at 37 °C.
Inoculate a single co-transformed colony in 5 mL of LB medium with antibiotics (25 µg/mL of kanamycin and 30 µg/mL of chloramphenicol).
Incubate overnight at 37 °C with shaking.
Dilute the primary culture (5 mL) into 500 mL of auto-induction medium containing antibiotics, 0.02% of L-arabinose and 1 mM of the unnatural amino acid PrK.
Incubate it at 37 °C for 24 h with shaking.
Aliquot 5 mL out of the 500 mL culture medium and centrifuge for 10 min at 5,000 x g.
Discard the supernatant and freeze the pellet at -20 °C.
Harvest cells from the remaining 495 mL by centrifugation for 10 min at 5,000 x g.
Discard the supernatant and freeze the pellet at -20 °C.
Resuspend 5 mL cell pellets into 250 μL of lysis buffer.
Transfer the resuspended cells into a 1.5 mL microtube.
Lyse cells by freezing the tubes in liquid nitrogen, then thawing them in a 42 °C bath.
Vortex at high speed for 30 seconds after each freeze-thaw cycle.
Repeat the freeze-thaw and vortex cycles three times.
Centrifuge samples at 17,000 x g for 10 minutes to eliminate cell debris.
Take 10 μL of the supernatant from centrifuged samples.
Add 5 μL of water and 5 μL of loading buffer to the supernatant.
Heat the sample mixture for 5 minutes at 100 °C.
Carry out SDS-PAGE and western blot analyses.
Resuspend cell pellets (from a 495 mL culture) into 20 mL of lysis buffer.
Add 5 μL of DNase I to the suspension.
Add 500 μL of lysozyme to the suspension.
Incubate the suspension at 37 °C for 30 minutes to allow lysis.
Sonicate the cells for 5 minutes (cycles of 5 s-5 s, amplitude 50%).
Remove cell debris by centrifuging at 20,000 x g for 30 minutes.
Filter the supernatant on a 0.45 μm filter.
Add Ni-NTA resin to the filtered suspension (500 μL for 500 mL of culture).
Mix gently at 4 °C for 1 hour.
Pour the suspension into a polypropylene column and collect the unbound fraction.
Wash the resin with 10 mL of washing buffer containing 50 mM Na2HPO4/NaH2PO4, 150 mM NaCl, and 10 mM imidazole.
Wash the resin again with 5 mL of washing buffer (50 mM Na2HPO4/NaH2PO4, 150 mM NaCl, and 20 mM imidazole).
Collect the wash fractions.
Elute the his-tagged protein with 1 mL of elution buffer (50 mM Na2HPO4/NaH2PO4, 150 mM NaCl, and 300 mM imidazole).
Repeat the elution step four times, collecting all the elution fractions.
Analyze the crude lysate and seven purification fractions by SDS-PAGE on a 12% acrylamide gel.
Combine the fractions containing pure His-tagged protein.
Dialyze the combined fractions against 1 L of TEV protease buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl, 0.5 mM EDTA, pH 8) overnight using a dialysis membrane with a cut-off MW of 6000-8000 Da.
Measure the concentration of the protein at 280 nm with a molar extinction coefficient of 37,360 cm^-1∙M^-1 and a molecular weight of 34.14 kDa for mPsaA.
Collect the protein sample into a 50 mL tube.
Add TEV buffer (50 mM Tris HCl, 0.5 mM EDTA, pH 8) to reach a final volume of 1 mL at a concentration of 2 mg/mL.
Add 100 µL of TEV protease for every 20 µg of protein to digest.
Include 50 µL of 0.1 M dithiothreitol (DTT).
Complete the mixture with TEV buffer up to a total volume of 5 mL.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C with slow shaking.
If digestion is not complete, add more TEV protease.
Incubate for longer time or at higher temperature up to 30 °C.
Dialyze the digested protein to remove EDTA at 4 °C overnight using a dialysis membrane (cut-off 6000-8000 Da) against phosphate buffer.
Incubate the mixture with Ni-NTA beads and mix gently for 1 h at 4 °C.
Pour the suspension into a polypropylene column.
Collect the unbound fraction.
Wash the column with 5 mL of washing buffer (50 mM Na2HPO4/NaH2PO4, 150 mM NaCl, 10 mM imidazole).
Elute the TEV protease and undigested protein by adding 5 mL of elution buffer (50 mM Na2HPO4/NaH2PO4, 150 mM NaCl, 300 mM imidazole) on the column.
Check the fractions for protein content at 280 nm and by SDS-PAGE analysis.
Load digested samples on an SDS PAGE with undigested protein as a control to check digestion efficiency.
Dialyze the digested protein against 1 L of click buffer (50 mM Na2HPO4/NaH2PO4, pH8) at 4 °C overnight using a dialysis membrane (cut-off 6000-8000 Da).
Measure the concentration of the protein at 280 nm with molar extinction coefficient and molecular weight of mPsaA.
Take 432.5 µL of PrK-mutated protein at a concentration of 57.8 µM into a 2 mL microtube.
Add 10 µL of 5 mM 6-hexachloro-fluorescein-azide to the microtube.
Add 2.5 µL of CuSO4 solution at 20 mM and 7.5 µL of THPTA at 50 mM to the mixture.
Add 25 µL of aqueous 100 mM aminoguanidine hydrochloride.
Add 25 µL of 20 mg/mL sodium ascorbate solution.
Close the tube, mix by inverting several times and incubate at room temperature for 2 h.
Stop the reaction by adding 50 µL of 0.5 M EDTA.
Take 15 µL of the reaction mixture and put it into a microtube.
Add 5 µL of loading buffer to the mixture.
Heat the mixture at 100 °C for 5 min.
Load the heated mixture into a 12% acrylamide gel.
Visualize the fluorescent conjugate on the gel under UV light at 312 nm.
Take 432.5 µL of PrK-mutated protein at 57.8 µM into a 2 mL microtube.
Add 10 µL of 5 mM Pn14TS-N321 in water to the tube.
Mix 2.5 µL of CuSO4 solution at 20 mM with 7.5 µL of THPTA at 50 mM and add this premix to the tube.
Add 25 µL of 100 mM aminoguanidine hydrochloride to the tube.
Add 25 µL of 20 mg/mL aqueous solution of sodium ascorbate to the tube.
Close the tube, mix by inverting several times and incubate at room temperature for 2 h.
Stop the reaction by adding 50 µL of 0.5 M EDTA to the tube.
Take 15 µL of samples and analyze by SDS-PAGE.
Purify the glycoconjugate by applying it to a steric exclusion agarose column, equilibrated with 100 mM PBS buffer at pH 7.3, using a flow rate of 0.8 mL/min with detection at 280 nm.
Collect the fractions containing the glycoconjugate from the column.
Dialyze the glycoconjugate against 1 L of H2O twice for 2 h and then overnight at 4 °C using a dialysis membrane (cut-off Mw 6000-8000 Da).
Freeze-dry the dialyzed glycoconjugate.
Store the freeze-dried glycoconjugate at -80 °C.
